structure.overview: This case involves a judicial review of the Social Security Tribunal's decision regarding whether Quebec paternity benefits and federal maternity/parental benefits are "corresponding types of benefits" under the Employment Insurance Regulations. The applicant, Mr. Ouimet, challenges the Appeal Division's decision that these benefits correspond, which affects his entitlement and repayment obligations. The Federal Court of Appeal upheld the Appeal Division's interpretation, dismissing the judicial review application.

sections.label: Context of the Regulations and legislative purpose
Court's conclusions on fairness and reasonableness

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court introduces the judicial review of the Social Security Tribunal's decision on whether Quebec paternity benefits and federal maternity/parental benefits are "corresponding types of benefits" under the Regulations.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains the importance of the issue, affecting benefit amounts and start dates, and whether Mr. Ouimet must repay $4,400 in benefits.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states it will uphold the Appeal Division's decision that Quebec paternity benefits are the same type as federal benefits when a child is born.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court summarizes undisputed facts: Mr. Ouimet accrued 600 hours, took Quebec paternity leave benefits Sept 17-Oct 21, then was laid off after returning to work.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Mr. Ouimet claimed federal regular benefits starting Dec 6, but the Commission deemed his benefit period to start Sept 17, the start of Quebec paternity benefits.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: If Mr. Ouimet had not received Quebec paternity benefits, he would have qualified for federal benefits in December due to 1,000 hours accrued; minimum hours required were 665.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court reproduces subsection 76.19(1.1) stating federal benefit periods align with provincial ones if claimant would be entitled to corresponding benefits under the Act.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Because Mr. Ouimet lacked minimum hours on Sept 17, the Commission denied federal benefits and demanded repayment of $4,400, upholding this on review.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The General Division reversed the Commission, ruling Quebec paternity and federal parental benefits are not corresponding, so no overpayment occurred.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The Appeal Division allowed the Commission's appeal, finding the General Division erred in law interpreting "corresponding types of benefits" as requiring identical benefits.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The Appeal Division explained "corresponding types" means benefits sharing common features, so Quebec paternity benefits are equivalent to federal benefits.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Mr. Ouimet seeks judicial review; the court's issue is whether the Appeal Division's decision to overturn the General Division's interpretation is reasonable.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court's role is to assess if the Appeal Division reasonably found the General Division erred in law, per the Vavilov standard of reasonableness.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The applicant argues the Appeal Division ignored Parliament's intent to prevent double benefits and that paternity benefits don't exist federally, so no corresponding benefits exist.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The applicant notes subsection 76.19(1) treats provincial benefits as federal when corresponding, affecting maximum weeks payable under the Act.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The applicant contends the Appeal Division erred by ignoring context, arguing Quebec paternity benefits differ from federal maternity/parental benefits and 2019 amendments aligned the plans.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Respondent's counsel raised new textual arguments at hearing about the phrase "corresponding types" referring only to maternity/parental benefits, urging harmonious interpretation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court rejects the respondent's new textual arguments as unacceptable.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes the Act favors claimants in ambiguity but requires plausible interpretations based on language, context, and purpose.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court concludes the Appeal Division reasonably found subsection 76.19(1.1) unambiguous and that the General Division erred in excluding paternity benefits as corresponding.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains "corresponding types" means resembling benefits, not identical, consistent with Regulations allowing provincial plans to differ from federal ones.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court dismisses the applicant's argument about phrase absence in other provisions as unfair and inappropriate to consider first on judicial review.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the Appeal Division's interpretation aligns with ordinary meaning, context, and Parliament's object, citing Supreme Court precedent on parental benefits.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court holds paternity benefits share the objective of maternity and parental benefits, allowing parents to care for newborns, thus are corresponding types.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The 2019 Act amendment supports the respondent by creating equivalent paternal benefits through shared parental weeks, showing no real difference.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states Part III.1 of the Regulations aims to implement provincial-federal agreements and ensure fairness, as shown by the Regulatory Impact Study.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Quebec Parental Insurance Plan pays benefits for maternity, paternity, parental, and adoption leave to support new parents.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Subsection 76.19(1) limits entitlement by reducing federal weeks if provincial benefits correspond to federal ones.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Subsection 76.19(1.1) deems benefit periods established under provincial law to begin the same week federally if corresponding benefits exist; added in 2010.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: These provisions aim to ensure consistency and fairness between provinces with provincial plans and federal employment insurance benefits.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court agrees with the General Division that the applicant cannot receive both Quebec paternity benefits and federal parental benefits for the same period, as it would violate regulations and be unfair.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes that allowing the claimant to receive regular benefits without accounting for prior paternity benefits would give an unfair advantage and contradict statutory wording and parliamentary intent.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the Appeal Division's ruling reasonable despite harsh consequences for the applicant, stating adjustments should be made by the Commission and Governor in Council if needed.
idea_list: adjustments responsibility to Commission and Governor in Council

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court dismisses the judicial review application without costs, with all three judges agreeing.
